// 01 The Story

Lake town,
small-town pulse.

Downtown runs a few walkable blocks. People know each other here — generations of them — and the water is the center of gravity. Buyers tell me the same thing over and over: it feels settled, safe, and a little charmed.

In 2025, public access to the lake opened at Lower Millennium Plaza Park, after the city chose not to fight the court ruling. Anyone can now get on the water from the park steps.

// Lake Days

The lake isn't scenery.
It's the lifestyle.

Summer weekends mean paddleboards at sunrise, kayaks crossing the water, and boats out for the July 4th fireworks. Winter is quieter: fireplaces, neighborhood dinners, the lake glassy under the fog.

The lake belongs to the whole town now. Since public access opened at Lower Millennium Plaza Park, getting on the water is no longer something you buy into — it's part of living here.

// 03 Schools & Amenities

An A+ district in
a town of parks.

The Lake Oswego School District serves about 6,800 students across seven elementary schools, two middle schools, and two high schools. Add a riverfront park scene, a downtown plaza, and miles of trails, and the calendar fills itself.
